rationale: Five behaviour-named fixtures pin the five ticket acceptance criteria plus two class-coverage fixtures (ItemDetailStoreTests, ItemDetailFetchServiceTests) required by CI0002 (TestCoverageAnalyzer) for the two new public classes, and ScrapeRunServiceTests is extended for the new additive constructor parameter. AC-1 (NewListingsGetItemDetailFetchedAfterARunTests) seeds a listing with a null DetailFetchedUtc and a URL served by a stub IScrapeClient returning the real captured item-active-m71344610988.html fixture, runs ItemDetailFetchService.FetchDetails against a real SQLite-backed ItemDetailStore and the real MercariItemPageParser, then asserts Description, ImageUrls, ShippingCost and Seller on the stored listing match the fixture's known values (the same values MercariItemPageParsesActiveItemDetailsTests already pins) and DetailFetchedUtc is set. AC-2 (SoldListingFromSearchGetsSoldDateAndHistoryFromDetailFetchTests) seeds a listing already marked Sold by a prior search (IsSold=true, SoldDate null, matching the ticket's stated gap) with a URL served by the real captured item-sold-m44688360101.html fixture, runs FetchDetails, and asserts the stored listing's SoldDate and SoldPrice equal the fixture's known sold values and exactly one ListingStatusChanges row with Source StatusUpdate exists for it. AC-3 (AlreadyDetailedListingIsNotRefetchedByLaterRunsTests) seeds a listing with DetailFetchedUtc already set and a stub client that fails the test if called, runs FetchDetails twice, and asserts the stub was never invoked and the stored DescriptionStatus/Description are unchanged from their pre-existing values. AC-4 (FailedItemFetchMarksListingFailedWithoutFailingTheRunTests) has two fixtures: one at the ItemDetailStore/ItemDetailFetchService level seeding two listings needing detail where the stub client throws for one URL and returns a real fixture for the other, asserting the failing listing's DescriptionStatus becomes 'failed' and DetailFetchedUtc is set (no further retries) while the succeeding listing still gets its detail fields populated, and Should_not_fail_the_run_when_a_detail_fetch_throws in ScrapeRunServiceTests asserting ScrapeRunService.Run still calls CompleteRun (not FailRun) when the substituted IItemDetailFetchService throws, proving a systemic detail-fetch failure is the only case that fails the run while per-listing failures are swallowed inside ItemDetailFetchService itself. AC-5 (DetailFetchHonoursConcurrencyAndPerRunCapTests) has two fixtures: Should_never_exceed_the_configured_concurrency_limit_while_fetching_details seeds more listings needing detail than MaxConcurrentDetailFetches and uses a concurrency-tracking stub IScrapeClient (gated by TaskCompletionSource so all requests are in flight simultaneously) that records the peak concurrent call count, asserting it never exceeds the configured limit and that all requests do eventually complete; Should_only_fetch_up_to_the_per_run_cap_and_leave_the_rest_for_a_later_run seeds more DetailFetchedUtc-null listings than MaxDetailFetchesPerRun against a real SQLite ItemDetailStore, runs FetchDetails once, and asserts exactly MaxDetailFetchesPerRun listings now have DetailFetchedUtc set while the remainder are still null (available to a later run). ItemDetailStoreTests and ItemDetailFetchServiceTests each directly invoke and assert on every public method of their respective class (GetListingsNeedingDetail, ApplyItemDetail, MarkDetailFetchFailed; FetchDetails) to satisfy CI0002. AC-6 (repo quality gate) is enforced by the pre-commit hook itself, not a named test. At base (before implementation) the command fails to compile: IItemDetailStore, ItemDetailStore, IItemDetailFetchService, ItemDetailFetchService, ListingDetailTarget and DetailFetchOptions do not exist, and ScrapeRunService's constructor does not accept an IItemDetailFetchService. No test reads git or working-tree state.
